system:
You are a computational cancer biologist searching CRISPR screen data for selective genetic dependencies: genes that cancer cells with a particular alteration (the biomarker) need more than other cancer cells do. Such genes are candidate drug targets with a built-in patient-selection strategy.

Work like a careful scientist:
1. Plan first with write_plan, and revise it as you learn.
2. Survey the data (genome_wide_top, scan_biomarker, scan_target) to generate candidate hypotheses.
3. Be sceptical before you believe a signal. Use inspect_association to check whether it is driven by one lineage or a disease subtype hiding inside a lineage, and whether the effect is large enough to matter. Ask whether the biology makes sense (paralog buffering, pathway dependence, oncogene addiction). A broadly essential target may lack a therapeutic window.
4. Check the literature with search_pubmed before registering, and judge novelty honestly.
5. Register only your best hypotheses (register_hypothesis). Registration is final and must come before replication. You have 5 replications, each of which must pass one-sided p < 0.01 in BOTH held-out Broad cell lines and independent Sanger screens.
6. Report honestly with submit_findings. A hypothesis is replicated only if replicate() said so. Negative results are results. Never let what you remember from the literature override what the data show.

You have at most 30 model turns. Batch independent tool calls in one turn.
task_prompt:
Mission: Search for synthetic-lethal paralog dependencies: genes whose loss (LOSS_ or MUT_ biomarkers) makes cells depend on a paralog or functional backup.

Goal: identify up to 5 candidate selective dependencies, and favour candidates that are NOT already well established in the literature, since rediscovering textbook biology is not the aim. Pre-register, replicate, and submit honest findings, including failures.

input.mechanism: DMXL1 and DMXL2 are paralogous rabconnectin-3 (mRAVE) subunits that assemble V-ATPase V1 onto V0; with DMXL2 lost, DMXL1 becomes the sole assembly factor, so V-ATPase function and lysosomal acidification depend on it.
ATP6V0E1/E2 are paralogous V-ATPase V0 e subunits; loss of E2 leaves E1 as the only e subunit, so V0 assembly and V-ATPase function depend on it.

NABP1 (hSSB2) and NABP2 (hSSB1) are redundant single-stranded DNA binding proteins in the SOSS complex that function in genome maintenance and Integrator-linked transcription; when NABP1 is lost, cells need NABP2.
CHPT1 and CEPT1 are paralogous enzymes that catalyse the last step of Kennedy-pathway phosphatidylcholine synthesis; when CHPT1 is lost, PC synthesis depends only on CEPT1.
SPAK (STK39) and OSR1 (OXSR1) are redundant WNK-activated kinases that control cation-chloride cotransporters and cell volume; when SPAK is lost, cells depend on OSR1.

input.summary: I surveyed lineage-adjusted LOSS_ and MUT_ biomarker→dependency pairs and picked paralog pairs that held up across lineages. Well-known pairs (RPP25/RPP25L, SMARCA4/SMARCA2, ARID1A/ARID1B) were skipped on purpose. I registered five hypotheses. Four replicated (one-sided p < 0.01 in both held-out Broad lines and Sanger screens): DMXL2→DMXL1, ATP6V0E2→ATP6V0E1, NABP1→NABP2 and CHPT1→CEPT1. STK39→OXSR1 replicated strongly in held-out Broad lines but could not be tested in Sanger (only 2 altered lines), so it does not meet the criterion. Caveats: altered-line counts are small for DMXL2 (5 held-out Broad, 3 Sanger) and CHPT1 (6 held-out Broad, 3 Sanger). DMXL2 and STK39 loss are enriched in blood cancers, and NABP1 loss in neuroblastoma and other neural tumours. CEPT1 is already needed by many unaltered lines, so its therapeutic window is narrower. Novelty is based on PubMed searches that found no paper on these specific pairs. Large published paralog screens may already contain some of them, so "not found" means no dedicated report, not proven novelty.

findings.claim: Cell lines that have lost DMXL2 depend selectively on its paralog DMXL1 (a V-ATPase assembly factor, part of rabconnectin/mRAVE). Discovery: 12 of 13 altered lines strongly dependent; replicated in held-out Broad (p=8e-15) and Sanger (p=2e-9) screens, though with few altered lines.

Cell lines that have lost ATP6V0E2 (mostly head and neck and oesophagus/stomach cancers) depend on the paralogous V-ATPase V0 e subunit ATP6V0E1 (effect about -0.9; held-out Broad p=1e-29, Sanger p=8e-26).

Cell lines that have lost NABP1 (hSSB2), enriched in neuroblastoma and embryonal tumours, depend more on its paralog NABP2 (hSSB1); replicated in held-out Broad (p=2e-12) and Sanger (p=3e-7) screens, with a smaller effect in Sanger.

Cell lines that have lost CHPT1 depend more on CEPT1 for the last step of phosphatidylcholine synthesis; replicated (held-out Broad p=5e-6, Sanger p=3e-7), but CEPT1 is also moderately needed in unaltered lines, so the window is narrower.

Cell lines that have lost STK39 (SPAK) depend on OXSR1 (OSR1). This replicated strongly in held-out Broad lines (p=6e-35), but Sanger had too few altered lines (2) to test, so it fails the pre-set criterion.
